title: Seascapes

description.main: The second volume in the Damiani and Matsumoto Editions series on Hiroshi Sugimoto, presenting the complete Seascapes series of more than 200 photographs in one book for the first time. 220 black-and-white reproductions with an essay by the sociologist Munesuke Mita. Clothbound with dust jacket, 272 pages.
description.extended:
Hiroshi Sugimoto's Seascapes, the second volume in the Damiani and Matsumoto Editions series on his work, reproduces the complete series of more than 200 seascapes in one book for the first time.

For more than thirty years Sugimoto has photographed seas around the world under one rule. The horizon sits at the exact centre of the frame, the water is calm, and the picture divides into two fields of tone, sea below and air above. Some plates are nearly white. In others the two halves darken until they almost merge. The 272-page clothbound book has a dust jacket and several fold-out plates, and carries 220 black-and-white reproductions, some not published before. Munesuke Mita, professor of sociology at the University of Tokyo, contributes an essay that reads the recent history of art against models of population growth and places Sugimoto's work within that account.

Sugimoto (b. 1948, Tokyo) has worked between Tokyo and New York since the 1970s. He has called photography a fossilization of time, and the Seascapes state that idea in its simplest form, as water and air seen much as the first people saw them. They sit alongside Dioramas and Theaters, published in the same format in 2014 and 2016. A later edition of this book added five photographs.
description.artist_bio: Hiroshi Sugimoto (b. 1948, Tokyo) moved to New York in 1974 and divides his time between Tokyo and New York. His work is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo, the National Gallery London, the National Museum of Modern Art Tokyo, the Smithsonian and Tate (per Artbook/D.A.P.).
description.exhibition_context: Getty record note: catalogue of an exhibition held at the Tripoli Gallery of Contemporary Art, Southampton, New York, August 27 to October 21, 2014. Not stated on the Damiani or D.A.P. pages.

notes: Shelf: Japanese. Damiani / Matsumoto Editions series. Second volume in the series (Dioramas 2014, Theaters 2016). First edition, 2015, 272 pages with fold-out plates and 220 black-and-white illustrations; essay by Munesuke Mita. The Getty record describes it as the catalogue of an exhibition at Tripoli Gallery, Southampton, New York, August 27 to October 21, 2014. A later Damiani edition (ISBN 9788862086240, 280 pages) adds five previously unpublished photographs. Damiani lists release August 2015; US release through Artbook/D.A.P. October 2015.
